question.text: Under SEBI regulations, how is the IDCW (Income Distribution cum Capital Withdrawal) option in a mutual fund scheme different from the erstwhile "Dividend" option?

answer.text: IDCW is a nomenclature change to clarify that distributions may include capital withdrawal and are not guaranteed — the underlying mechanism remains the same
IDCW provides tax-free distributions unlike the old dividend option which was taxable
IDCW guarantees a fixed periodic payout unlike the old dividend option which was discretionary
IDCW is available only for debt schemes while the old dividend option was available for all schemes

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM Series V-A workbook (p150), IDCW payouts are not assured, the NAV is adjusted to the extent of the payout, and investors must be informed that distributions can include a portion of their own capital. Pages 158-159 cover the post-2020 position that dividend income from mutual funds is taxable in the hands of investors and the April 1, 2021 disclosure splitting distributions into the income-distribution and capital-withdrawal components. The Trap: The IDCW renaming did not introduce a tax-free distribution (Option B) or a guaranteed/fixed periodic payout (Option C), and it is not restricted to debt schemes (Option D). It is a disclosure change clarifying that payouts may include both income and capital and are not assured. Note: Two facts work together: IDCW payouts reduce NAV by the distribution amount, and the dividend income is taxable in the investor's hands at applicable slab rates (p150, p158-p159).
